Explanation: Meaning, scope, and verification are all clear; a tester can confirm the pilot's display shows current position. Update rate is separately specified in SFMC-REQ-002.
Fully quantified (500 ms), single, mode-conditioned, and directly testable.
Clear single capability with an obvious pass/fail test (can the pilot select a destination).

The terms 'safe' and 'efficient' are not defined anywhere in the SRS (the document's own Open Items #1 flags 'definition of a safe route' as unresolved). A tester has no objective criterion to check a calculated route against, so this requirement is not verifiable as written.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder input to define 'safe' (e.g., minimum obstacle/collision clearance, restricted-zone avoidance rules) and 'efficient' (e.g., time or fuel optimization criterion) before this can be made verifiable; we do not have enough information to propose specific criteria.

Explanation: Clear trigger condition (Autopilot enabled) and clear resulting behavior (control propulsion to follow the route); testable by observing autopilot behavior.

'Reasonably close' is a subjective distance with no numeric tolerance; Open Item #2 explicitly flags this as an undefined term. Different reviewers/testers could disagree on whether a given arrival point satisfies the requirement.
Proposed Revision: Requires a stakeholder-defined arrival tolerance (e.g., maximum distance from destination coordinates) to replace 'reasonably close'; no specific value can be proposed without further input (see Open Item #2).

Explanation: Clear, single, continuously-verifiable monitoring obligation.
Quantified threshold (15%) with a clear, testable display behavior.
Quantified threshold (5%) with two clearly coupled, testable response actions under one trigger.

The sentence bundles two distinct obligations: notifying the pilot (clear and testable) and taking 'appropriate corrective action' (undefined -- no list of failure modes or corresponding actions is given anywhere in the SRS). The second half cannot be tested without knowing what action is 'appropriate' for each failure type.
Proposed Revision: Split into two requirements: (1) notify the pilot of an engine failure -- already verifiable as written -- and (2) a requirement enumerating the specific corrective action(s) per failure mode, which requires propulsion-engineering input to define; we cannot propose the specific actions here.

Explanation: Clear single display behavior with an objective trigger (spacecraft within sensor range).
Clear single capability, easily tested.
Well-scoped, itemized list of exactly what must be displayed for a selected target; no ambiguity about completeness.
Clear precondition (pilot authorization) and clear prohibited behavior; directly testable.

'Friendly spacecraft' has no defined classification criteria (Open Item #10 explicitly says friend/hostile determination criteria don't exist yet), so a tester cannot determine which targets fall under this restriction. Separately, the absolute 'never' cannot be proven true by any finite test suite -- only that no failure was observed during testing.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder-defined friend/hostile classification criteria (see Open Item #10) before 'friendly spacecraft' can be objectively determined; also recommend rephrasing the absolute 'never' as a defined safety interlock (e.g., 'shall block weapon release unless target IFF status = Friendly') so it is verifiable once classification criteria exist.

Explanation: 'Extremely accurate' is a subjective, unquantified term with no defined metric (e.g., miss distance, hit probability) or range/conditions; Open Item #7 explicitly flags targeting accuracy as unresolved. There is no way to write a pass/fail test for this requirement as written.
Proposed Revision: Requires a stakeholder-defined accuracy metric (e.g., a specific miss-distance or hit-probability figure at a stated range) to replace 'extremely accurate' (see Open Item #7); no numeric value can be proposed without further input.

Explanation: Clear trigger (identified incoming threat) and clear resulting display behavior.

'Greatest danger' implies a threat-ranking calculation, but the SRS defines no criteria (e.g., proximity, closing speed, warhead type) for computing relative danger among simultaneous threats. Without that, a tester cannot verify the system picked the correct highest-priority threat.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder-defined threat-ranking criteria (e.g., time-to-impact, closing velocity, warhead lethality) to make 'greatest danger' objectively determinable; we cannot propose the specific ranking algorithm here.

Explanation: Clear mode-triggered behavior (Combat mode entered -> shields activate); directly testable.
Clear trigger (automatic defense enabled + incoming guided weapon) and clear response; testable.

'Quickly' and 'dangerous' are both undefined and unquantified. There is no response-time threshold and no criterion for which threats count as 'dangerous' (as distinct from the general threats already covered by SFMC-REQ-017/018/020), so this requirement cannot be objectively tested.
Proposed Revision: Requires a stakeholder-defined response-time threshold and a definition of 'dangerous threat' to replace 'respond quickly'; no specific value can be proposed without further input.

Explanation: Clear single pilot capability.
Clear, testable notification behavior on a well-defined trigger (new message received).
Clear single capability to flag an outgoing message.

'Important' communications are not defined anywhere in the SRS (Open Item #4 flags this explicitly), so it is unclear which messages this requirement applies to. 'Securely encrypted' also names no required algorithm/standard (Open Item #9), so a tester cannot check compliance.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder input to define which communications qualify as 'important' and which encryption standard/algorithm is required (see Open Item #9); we cannot propose a specific standard here.

Explanation: Clear, itemized scope of which subsystems are monitored; no ambiguity.
Quantified (1 second), clear trigger and display behavior; directly testable.
Clear, single record-keeping obligation; contents specified separately in SFMC-REQ-029.
Well-scoped itemized list of required fault-log fields; no ambiguity about completeness.

'Critical fault' is undefined (Open Item #3 flags this explicitly) -- the SRS gives no criteria distinguishing a 'critical' fault from the general faults already covered by SFMC-REQ-027/028/029. 'Immediately' is also an unquantified timing term, in contrast to the explicit 1-second bound the SRS gives for general fault display in SFMC-REQ-027.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder-defined criteria for what qualifies as a 'critical fault' (see Open Item #3) and a specific maximum notification latency (the SRS already sets 1 second for general fault display in SFMC-REQ-027, which stakeholders may wish to reuse or override for critical faults); we cannot assume that value applies here without confirmation.

Explanation: Clear, single, testable capability tied to a specific control.

'Nonessential spacecraft functions' is not defined, so it's unclear which functions this deprioritizes. More significantly, 'life-support' is never introduced as an SFMC subsystem or interface anywhere in Sections 1.2 or 2 (External Interfaces list Navigation, Propulsion, Weapons, Defensive, Communications, Pilot Display/Controls, and Health Monitoring only), so it's unclear whether the SFMC has any actual interface to a life-support system to prioritize in the first place.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder clarification of whether a Life-Support System is within SFMC scope (it is not listed among the subsystems in Sections 1.2/2) and, if so, addition of it to the system overview/interfaces; also requires a definition of 'nonessential spacecraft functions' and how the prioritization is to be implemented/verified.

Explanation: 'Seriously damaged' has no defined threshold or triggering condition, and 'safest destination' is undefined (Open Item #5 covers the related 'safe location' concept but this specific wording is not separately resolved). A tester cannot determine when this requirement should activate or what output would satisfy it.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder-defined criteria for 'seriously damaged' (which fault/damage conditions trigger this behavior) and for 'safest destination' (see Open Item #5); we cannot propose specific criteria here.

Explanation: 'Safe location' is undefined (Open Item #5 flags this explicitly). Additionally, 'shall be capable of' is a weaker modal than the plain 'shall' used elsewhere in the SRS -- it is unclear whether the requirement mandates that the SFMC actually perform automatic emergency flight, or merely that the capability exists (which could be satisfied even if the feature is never exercised).
Proposed Revision: Requires the same 'safe location' criteria needed for SFMC-REQ-033 (see Open Item #5); also recommend clarifying whether this requirement mandates that the SFMC actually execute emergency autopilot flight or merely have the capability available.

Explanation: Clear and testable: pilot input can be checked to take precedence over automatic control in any mode.
Quantified (30 seconds) startup requirement; directly testable.

'Without noticeable delay' has no numeric bound; Open Item #8 explicitly flags the maximum acceptable command response time as unresolved. Different observers would disagree on what counts as 'noticeable,' so there is no objective pass/fail test.
Proposed Revision: Requires a stakeholder-defined maximum response latency (e.g., in milliseconds) to replace 'without noticeable delay' (see Open Item #8); this is the same category of gap as the Sprint Packet's own SR-042 example -- a numeric value should come from stakeholders, not be invented here.

Explanation: Quantified (10 Hz) refresh requirement; directly testable.
Quantified (72-hour) duration requirement; directly testable via endurance testing.

An absolute 'never crash' cannot be verified through testing -- testing can only show the software has not yet been observed to crash, not that it can never crash. No reliability target, MTBF, or bounded-fault-rate criterion is given that a tester could actually check against.
Proposed Revision: Recommend replacing the absolute 'never crash' with a defined, testable reliability target (e.g., a maximum permitted crash rate/MTBF, or a bounded automatic-recovery time) since an absolute 'never' cannot be proven by finite testing; the specific target must come from a reliability/safety stakeholder.

Explanation: 'Recoverable' software fault is not defined -- the SRS gives no criteria for which fault classes are considered recoverable versus unrecoverable, so a tester has no basis for selecting which faults to inject during recovery testing. No maximum recovery time is given either, unlike the explicit 1-second bound given for fault display in SFMC-REQ-027.
Proposed Revision: Requires a definition of which fault classes are considered 'recoverable' and a maximum recovery time bound; we cannot propose specific criteria or a time value without further input from the fault-management design.

Explanation: 'Important mission data' is undefined. SFMC-REQ-045 does define the contents of the mission log, but this requirement doesn't reference that list or otherwise say what data counts as 'important,' so a tester cannot determine what data loss would constitute a violation.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder-defined criteria for what counts as 'important mission data' (e.g., cross-reference to the mission-log contents in SFMC-REQ-045); we cannot propose a specific definition here.

Explanation: 'Whenever possible' is an unfalsifiable escape clause -- any instance where the SFMC fails to continue operating after a subsystem loss could be excused as 'not possible' with no way to disprove that claim. The SRS gives no enumerated list of subsystem-loss combinations under which continued operation is actually required.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholders to replace the unfalsifiable 'whenever possible' qualifier with an enumerated set of subsystem-loss combinations under which continued operation is required; we cannot propose that matrix here.

Explanation: Clear, single obligation to maintain a log; contents specified separately in SFMC-REQ-045.
Well-scoped itemized list of events to be logged; no ambiguity about completeness.
Clear, single, testable field requirement for every log entry.

'Sufficient storage for an entire mission' has no numeric value; Open Item #6 explicitly flags the required log storage capacity as unresolved. A tester cannot check whether an implementation's log storage satisfies this requirement without a concrete capacity figure.
Proposed Revision: Requires a stakeholder-defined storage capacity (e.g., in MB/GB), derived from the maximum mission duration (72 hours per SFMC-REQ-039) and the expected log entry rate/size; no specific number can be proposed without that input.

Explanation: Clear precondition/gate behavior; directly testable (attempt operation with/without authorization).
Clear, single, testable rejection behavior for a well-defined trigger.

'State-of-the-art' is a subjective, moving-target term with no fixed, checkable meaning (what is state-of-the-art today may not be next year), and it names no specific algorithm or standard; Open Item #9 explicitly flags the required cybersecurity algorithms/standards as unresolved.
Proposed Revision: Requires stakeholder-defined applicable security standards/algorithms (see Open Item #9) to replace 'state-of-the-art,' which is not independently verifiable; we cannot propose a specific standard here.

Explanation: Clear, single deployment constraint, appropriate for the Constraints section; directly testable (does it run on the named platform).
Clear, single deployment/interface constraint; directly testable.
Clear precondition (Standby mode) and clear testable capability (install update).
Clear, single, testable verification obligation before installation, even though the specific integrity-check method is left to design (appropriately, as an implementation detail).
